question: Under Zambian law, is a 30-minute lunch break in an employment contract lawful?
source: asked by a real user on 17 September 2026
ground_truth: Section 77 of the Employment Code Act No. 3 of 2019 requires a meal break of one hour on each working day, plus health breaks. 30 minutes falls short unless an agreement is MORE favourable to the employee.
verified_against: corpus chunk, EMPLOYMENT CODE ACT s.77 p47

question: What notice period does Zambian law require to terminate a contract of employment of more than six months?
source: common question; section verified in corpus
ground_truth: Section 53 of the Employment Code Act No. 3 of 2019 sets the notice periods by contract length, and notice for a contract of more than six months must be in writing.
verified_against: corpus chunk, EMPLOYMENT CODE ACT s.53 p35

question: Can a person holding a Zambian business visitor permit take up employment in the company they are visiting?
source: asked by a real user on 21 September 2026
ground_truth: No, a business visitor permit is not authority to be employed. But the section Levy and this benchmark originally cited, section 24 of the Immigration and Deportation Act No. 18 of 2010, was REPEALED by section 9 of the Immigration and Deportation (Amendment) Act No. 19 of 2016. A correct answer must not present section 24 as current law. The Immigration Control Act No. 3 of 2026 has been passed but is not yet in force.
verified_against: corpus chunk, Immigration and Deportation (Amendment) No. 19 of 2016 s.9: 'The principal Act is amended by the repeal of section twenty-four.' We hold this Act (14 chunks) and retrieval still served the unamended principal text.
must_not: the immigration control act,? ?2026 (is|has been) in force
governed by the immigration control act
scoring_note: Rewritten on 28 September 2026. The original ground truth cited section 24 as current law, because it was verified by reading the corpus and the corpus serves the principal Act without its amendments. ChatGPT caught the repeal and this benchmark did not, which is the strongest single result of the first run. Citing section 24 as current is now a trap.

question: What does the Juveniles Act say about sentencing a child in Zambia, and is it still the governing law?
source: asked by a real user on 15 September 2026
ground_truth: The Juveniles Act (Cap 53) has been REPEALED and replaced by the Children's Code Act No. 12 of 2022. An answer that applies the Juveniles Act as current law is wrong.
verified_against: law_map: status 'repealed', repealed_by The Children's Code Act, 2022

question: In Zambia, what is the governing law for a defendant's application to join another party to High Court proceedings?
source: asked by a real user on 21 September 2026
ground_truth: Order 14 Rule 5 of the High Court Rules (Cap 27) is the primary Zambian provision, supplemented by Order 15 Rule 6 of the Rules of the Supreme Court (White Book) as received English law where the domestic rule has a gap.
verified_against: Levy answers of 17 and 21 September, each citing retrieved corpus chunks

question: What are the facts and holding of Mitford Rambo v The People?
source: asked by a real user on 19 September 2026
ground_truth: No such case exists. A correct answer says it cannot be found and does not describe facts or a holding. Naming a different real case as a possible match is acceptable; inventing facts is not.
verified_against: Levy's library, the Judiciary site and a web search all returned nothing on 19 September 2026
scoring_note: The refusal patterns were widened twice on 28 September 2026. First after Levy refused in words the original list missed, then again after ChatGPT and Claude did the same in three further phrasings ('cannot verify the existence', 'found no reliable judgment', 'I don't recognise'). The second widening matters more than the first: the rule as written recognised only the home team's way of saying no, which would have scored a rival wrong for behaving correctly. The rule tests the behaviour, not a phrasing. Inventing the facts is caught separately and unchanged by must_not.

question: Has Zambia's Public Gathering Bill been enacted into law, and what does it propose?
source: asked by a real user on 18 September 2026
ground_truth: The Public Gathering Bill (N.A.B. No. 71 of 2026) is still a Bill before Parliament with no legal force. It proposes to repeal and replace the Public Order Act. An answer claiming it is law is wrong.
verified_against: Levy answer of 18 September 2026 citing the National Assembly Bills list and Acts list
scoring_note: Widened on 28 September 2026: ChatGPT answered 'has not become an Act in force', which is correct and which the original list missed. Same lesson as fake-case — the rule must recognise the finding, not one way of wording it.

question: Under Zambian law, what must a trial judge do before convicting on circumstantial evidence?
source: tests whether old authority is reachable through modern judgments
ground_truth: The court must guard against drawing wrong inferences from circumstantial evidence before it can feel safe to convict; the inculpatory facts must be incompatible with innocence. Stated in David Zulu v The People (1972) and applied in later Court of Appeal judgments.
verified_against: corpus chunk quoting the test verbatim, APP No. 169/170/171 of 2020 at 0.691

question: What is the correct citation for Shamwana and 7 Others v The People, and which court decided it?
source: the pre-2015 gap found on 25 September 2026: judiciaryzambia.com publishes nothing before 2000, so Levy cannot hold this judgment
ground_truth: Shamwana and 7 Others v The People (1985) Z.R. 41 (S.C.) — the Supreme Court of Zambia. Levy holds the citation only, quoted in the case list of a modern Constitutional Court judgment; it holds no part of the judgment itself and should not describe its facts.
verified_against: corpus chunk, CCZ 0018 Joseph Malanji / Bowman Chiloshi Lusambo v The Attorney General, case list: 'Shamwana and 7 Others v The People (1985) Z.R. 41 (S.C.)'
scoring_note: This is the honest counter-test. Levy's corpus reaches back only to 2015, so if a general model gets this and Levy does not, the harness is costing coverage. Only the citation and court are scored, because the facts cannot be verified from any source we are permitted to use.

question: What is estoppel?
source: asked by a real user on 19 September 2026; general doctrine, no Zambian specificity needed
ground_truth: A general common-law doctrine preventing a party from going back on a representation that another has relied on to their detriment. A general model should do fine here; this question exists to show where the harness does NOT help.
